in_text_mentions: A routine abdominal ultrasound was performed, which revealed normal liver parenchyma, without focal lesions, with discrete dilation of the intrahepatic bile ducts. There was thickening of the gallbladder wall, with visualization of hyperechoic structures inside it with hypoechoic center lines like a rail, creating a tubular coiled appearance, without acoustic shadowing, and with apparent writhing movements (Figure 1). The main bile duct was normal. These imaging findings were compatible with biliary ascariasis. A chest radiograph was performed, and it did not show any significant alterations.
